findings.where: Screens 4, 8 and 10, the SHOW instructions "Tap -Q1", "Open -Q2, then tap -Q4" and "Open -Q13, then close -Q23"
findings.what: The demonstration has already made each move by the time he reads the words, so doing what they say undoes it (on screen 10 tapping -Q13 brings up "Interlocked. Open -Q23 first.", on screen 8 tapping -Q2 brings up the synchronise card, on screen 4 -Q1 recloses): word each as what he watches and then what he may try ("Watch -Q13 open and -Q23 close. Tap either one to try it yourself."), or hold the demonstration until his tap.

findings.where: Screens 11 and 13, the result card "... is isolated", and the finish line
findings.what: No screen says the drawing only tells him where to lock off and never that the part is dead, because the prove-dead line and the control or heater supply the drawing leaves off sit only in practice.text, which a steps lesson does not show: add one sentence to screen 11's Why or the finish, such as "The drawing tells you what to lock off. Prove it dead at the pump before you start."

findings.where: Screen 2 read sentence and its sweep, against screen 3's typed answer
findings.what: Screen 2's read ends "with the four sources ringed", and its sweep rings all four sources, battery included, one screen before screen 3 asks him to type how many there are, which gives away the battery-at-the-bottom slip the puzzle is built on: drop "four" from the read and the rings from the sweep, and let the source lines simply light first.

For up to 4 s the sweep drops every line to pale and every lamp to "No supply", under a key that defines those as Dead and No supply, while the board's state has not changed: show the reading order with the amber halo over the bold lines and leave the live state alone.

No screen says the thick lines are the busbars or that a DC line stands for a pair, and none names a symbol (the breaker's cross, the isolator's bar, the transformer's two circles, the charger's box with ~ over =, the battery's plates) or shows the US forms the brief promised: add "The thick lines are the busbars." to screen 2 and one short symbols sentence to screen 6, or give the symbols one SHOW screen.
The demonstration opens -Q2 before it closes -Q4, but the words never say why, so the link to screen 1 is skipped: add "With -Q2 open, section B is dead, so -Q4 can close without synchronising."

findings.where: Screen 9 task and its hint for "Nothing, section B is dead"
findings.what: Screen 9 asks what screen 8's demonstration and say line have just shown ("Section B is ... fed from -G1 through the tie"), so it tests memory, and its hint "-Q4 is drawn open, but now it is closed" contradicts the sheet, which still shows -Q4 open before Check: ask a new case, such as -G1 stopped and -Q3 closed with the question "What feeds -M1?", and word the hint "You have closed -Q4. Follow the line through it."

"A normally open breaker carries nothing past it until it closes. Either side of it can still be live. Then it carries power like any other." muddles the order because "Then" points back two sentences: write "A normally open breaker carries nothing across until it closes. Once closed, it carries power like any other."

findings.where: Screens 11 and 13, the Board / Isolate switch
findings.what: The switch appears with no word on any screen about what it does, and before Check pressing Board only removes the chosen load's highlight: add to screen 11's task "In Isolate mode, each device you lock off gets a padlock.", or show the switch only after Check.
The readout shows "?" on a question about sources, which suggests the answer is a count of loads: hide that readout on screen 3, or show its real value there.

findings.where: Screen 1 (the opener) and the "As drawn" caption
findings.what: The opener does not ring -Q4, the device it asks about, though screens 5 and 7 ring theirs, and no screen asks "what state is this drawn in?" or says why the caption is there (a single-line diagram does not say how the plant is run), as the brief planned: ring -Q4 and add a caption sentence such as "The drawing does not say which breakers are kept open. A note like this one does."

findings.where: Analogy, breaks: "Only the diagram shows every way in."
findings.what: This overclaims, because a diagram can be out of date and the plant's own labels also show the ways in: write "An up-to-date diagram is the one place that shows every way in."

findings.where: The sheet, load lamps of -M1, -M3 and -M2
findings.what: The lamps of -M1 and -M3 sit to the right of their loads and the lamp of -M2 to the left, so the -M3 and -M2 lamps face each other across -Q23's line, and on screen 12, where only -M2 goes dark, he can read the wrong lamp: put every lamp on the same side of its load.
